In `length_of_largest_common_substring`, `max_length` starts at `0` and is updated only inside `if dp[i][j] > max_length:` by setting `max_length = dp[i][j]`. So before any later evaluation of that condition, `max_length` is the largest previously seen matching-substring length. But `dp[i][j]` at the current cell is just the current diagonal extension `dp[i-1][j-1] + 1` when the current characters match, and it can be smaller than an earlier maximum. For example, after the code has already found a long common substring, a later isolated 1-character match will make `dp[i][j] = 1` while `max_length` remains larger, so `dp[i][j] >= max_length` does not always hold.
